newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end at new high after morning stumble.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end at new high after morning stumble.

text.p: Dutch shares recovered from a sickly morning as Greenspan's latest comments soothed markets worldwide, allowing the strong dollar to drive certain shares to new peaks and the index to a new closing record, traders said.
The AEX index of 25 leading shares ended up 1.83 points, or 0.24 percent, at 755.23 points, a new closing high. It earlier reached an intra-day peak of 756.39.

The market briefly flirted with the highs shortly after the opening, but soon slid down from Tuesday's record close. It had to wait for Greenspan's latest comments that he had not wished to "jawbone" the U.S. market to return to positive territory.

Dutch traders said the comments from the chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve had clearly encouraged the market up, but his frequent statements had increased nervousness. In the Dutch share market the effect had been to limit volumes.
"It's making people more scared. Now he says the outlook for the stock market is difficult to forecast. It's really not good for his reputation," one trader said.
Nevertheless, the comments did allow Wednesday's few star performers to pull the market out of its trough.
In the vanguard was Philips which announced the retirement Wednesday of executive vice president Jan Tollenaar.
Philips' shares rose 2.60 guilders to 92.50, just off the intra-day high of 92.80.
"(The retirement) suggests that (chairman Cor) Boonstra is getting what he wants. The Americans particularly prefer him to his predecessors," one trader said.
Royal Dutch was another solid performer, helped by both the strong dollar and firming oil prices. Its shares rose by 2.40 guilders to 338.40.
A few other companies came through well towards the end of the day, among them chemicals firm DSM and retailer Ahold which releases full year figures on Thursday.
Traders said DSM's rise of 4.00 guilders to 196.80 was probably a delayed reaction to its announcement last week that it would raise its dividend and encourage longer term investors.
"There's no particular news, but it's just a sign of steadily increasing interest (in DSM)," one trader said.

Meanwhile, Ahold put on 2.40 guilders to 132.20 ahead of Thursday's results announcement, with the consolidation of U.S. supermarket chain Stop & Shop expected to boost fourth quarter profit by up to 60 percent.
"The story with Ahold is really rather promising," a trader said.
